units.title: The literal full precision, including its residual identity block
units.statement: Within the standing range kappa>=4 and 3<=n<=d, put k=floor(d/n). For every tuple of k real orthogonal n by n matrices, define the d by d precision as diag(A_O1,...,A_Ok,I_(d-kn)), where A_O=((kappa+1)/2)I-((kappa-1)/4)(O+O^T).
assumptions: d and n are natural dimensions; kappa is a real number.
n>=3, n<=d and kappa>=4 are the source standing range.
O is a tuple indexed by Fin(d/n), with each matrix in the full real orthogonal group on Fin n.
The literal algebraic definition extends to every natural d,n and real kappa; spectral and minimizer theorems retain the source range.

steps.title: Use consecutive coordinates
steps.text: Mathlib indexes equal blocks by (inner coordinate, block). Swap these indices before flattening, so the original coordinate is inner+n*block. The residual coordinate starts at k*n.
steps.lean: The private blockCoordinates uses prodComm, finProdFinEquiv, sumCongr, finSumFinEquiv and finCongr.

steps.title: Retain the residual identity
steps.text: Euclidean division gives d=k*n+r with r=d mod n=d-k*n. Reindex the literal block diagonal to Fin d. When r=0, Fin0 is empty and no residual coordinate is introduced.
steps.lean: blockPrecision applies Matrix.reindex to fromBlocks (blockDiagonal ...) 0 0 1; no padding or fallback replaces the residual block.

units.title: Sum the actual single-block estimates in the original coordinates
units.statement: For n>=3,n<=d,kappa>=4 and every tuple of floor(d/n) real orthogonal n by n matrices, the literal d-dimensional precision A is symmetric and every x in R^d satisfies x^T x<=x^T A x<=kappa x^T x. Hence A belongs to the source admissible precision class.
units.formula: A=A^\top,\qquad \|x\|_2^2\le x^\top A x\le\kappa\|x\|_2^2\quad(\forall x\in\mathbb R^d)
assumptions: d and n are natural dimensions; kappa is a real number.
n>=3, n<=d and kappa>=4 are the source standing range.
O is a tuple indexed by Fin(d/n), with each matrix in the full real orthogonal group on Fin n.

steps.title: Symmetry survives block assembly
steps.text: The existing single-block theorem proves each A_Oj symmetric. Block diagonal assembly, the identity tail and the coordinate equivalence preserve real Hermitianity, which is symmetry.
steps.lean: hB uses singleBlockPrecision_regular, isHermitian_blockDiagonal_iff and IsHermitian.fromBlocks; IsHermitian.reindex returns the result on Fin d.

steps.title: Split the two quadratic forms
steps.text: Pull x back through the exact coordinate equivalence. Its blocks are v_j and its residual is z. Matrix-vector multiplication has no cross-block terms, so both expressions split into finite sums.
steps.lean: hchange proves the quadratic form is preserved under reindex. hvec, hnorm and hquad expand the actual fromBlocks/blockDiagonal matrix, using finite sum reordering.

steps.title: Sum the existing bounds and handle the tail
steps.text: Apply the compiled single-block lower and upper bounds to each v_j and sum them. The standing kappa>=4 implies kappa>=1, so the residual squared norm is at most kappa times itself. Empty residual sums also cover kn=d.
steps.lean: hlo and hupp call singleBlockPrecision_regular inside the proof; htail derives its coefficient condition from hκ. No spectral estimate is a public hypothesis.

units.title: The quadratic potential has its unique minimum at zero
units.statement: Under the same n>=3,n<=d,kappa>=4 and orthogonal tuple assumptions, the actual potential f_A(x)=(1/2)x^T A x has f_A(0)=0, is nonnegative for every x, and equals zero if and only if x=0. Thus its unique minimizer is0 and its minimum value is0.
assumptions: d and n are natural dimensions; kappa is a real number.
n>=3, n<=d and kappa>=4 are the source standing range.
O is a tuple indexed by Fin(d/n), with each matrix in the full real orthogonal group on Fin n.

steps.title: The origin has value zero
steps.text: The literal quadratic expression vanishes at the zero vector.
steps.lean: The first conjunct unfolds the displayed potential and simplifies zero matrix-vector and dot products.

steps.title: The lower spectral bound gives nonnegativity
steps.text: Apply the actual full-precision theorem to the same x. Since its coordinate squared sum is nonnegative, so is the potential.
steps.lean: hlow is produced by blockPrecision_regular, with the same hn,hnd,hκ and O. hnonneg is the finite sum of coordinate squares.

steps.title: Zero energy forces every coordinate to vanish
steps.text: If f_A(x)=0, the lower bound forces the sum of squared coordinates to be0. Each nonnegative summand is at most this sum, hence each coordinate is0. Conversely x=0 has zero energy. Combined with nonnegativity, this gives strict positivity for x!=0 and the unique minimum.
steps.lean: The proof uses Finset.single_le_sum and mul_self_eq_zero. The theorem packages nonnegativity and the exact zero set; this is equivalent to the source unique-minimizer conclusion.
